_meta.purpose: Real-world Indian field-experiment take-up rates to backtest the decision model (persona_math.evaluate_offer). Each scenario maps a study population to decision_model() params and the offer to evaluate_offer() params, with the OBSERVED take-up to compare against.
_meta.status: STARTER — figures are approximate and drawn from widely-cited development-economics studies. VERIFY each `observed_take_up` and citation against the primary paper before using as a hard model-acceptance gate. The model is calibrated for recurring-cost / uncertain-benefit offers (insurance-like), so financial scenarios are primary; others are DIRECTIONAL.
_meta.how_predicted_is_computed: For each scenario we build the decision_model with the listed population params across many RNG seeds, run evaluate_offer with the listed offer params, and average P_accept. We then report |predicted - observed| and a directional pass.

scenarios.label: Rainfall/weather index insurance, smallholder farmers, full price
scenarios.source: Cole, Gine, Tobacman, Topalova, Townsend, Vickery — rainfall insurance demand in Andhra Pradesh/Gujarat; take-up famously low (~5-30%) at market price. VERIFY exact figure.

scenarios.label: Rainfall insurance with a large price discount / subsidy
scenarios.source: Same literature: take-up is strongly price-elastic; a steep discount roughly doubles uptake. VERIFY exact figure.

scenarios.label: Voluntary micro health-insurance premium, low-income urban
scenarios.source: Voluntary health micro-insurance demand in India is low double-digits absent subsidy/mandate. VERIFY against specific RSBY/SEWA studies.

scenarios.label: Commitment savings product offered to low-income savers
scenarios.source: Commitment-savings take-up among the poor is typically ~25-30% when offered (cf. Ashraf-Karlan-Yin SEED, Philippines; Indian analogues vary). DIRECTIONAL — VERIFY.

scenarios.label: Recurring paid digital service offered to urban salaried (control contrast)
scenarios.source: No single RCT — included as a CONTRAST: a low-scarcity, high-capital persona should accept a growth-framed recurring service at a materially higher rate than a high-scarcity farmer accepts insurance. Tests directional sensitivity to capital/scarcity, not an exact number.

_sweeps_note: One-variable monotonicity sweeps are the rigorous directional test: hold a base population+offer fixed, vary ONE param, assert P(accept) moves the empirically-correct direction. Cross-scenario comparisons confound multiple params and must not be used for directional validation.

sweeps.rationale: Higher recurring cost ⇒ larger loss term ⇒ P(accept) must DECREASE monotonically.
Higher scarcity ⇒ lower present-bias beta (steeper discounting of the uncertain gain) ⇒ P(accept) must DECREASE.
Higher benefit value ⇒ larger prob-weighted gain ⇒ P(accept) must INCREASE.
A loss-framed 'shield' (protect what you have) is accepted more than a gain-framed 'growth' offer, all else equal (prospect-theory loss aversion).
